exposure: Deeply impacted fetal head during cesarean delivery
outcome: Causes of deeply impacted fetal head
Risks associated with deeply impacted fetal head
cohort: 200 pregnant women with a singleton fetus whose head was deeply impacted in the pelvis and underwent cesarean section.
finding: The study identified primigravida and fetal head malposition as the most common risk factors for impacted fetal head, while deep transverse arrest was the most frequent cause, leading to various maternal and fetal complications.
